item.title: Radiation Conditions and Uniqueness Theorems for Open Wave-guide Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.20891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We state radiation conditions and prove a variety of uniqueness theorem for models of wave-guide networks, including acoustic wave-guide networks, and electromagnetic wave-guide networks described by the time harmonic Maxwell equations. To analyze Maxwell wave-guide networks we need to establish generalizations of the Mourre estimates from [29, 32].
item.dc:creator: Charles L. Epstein, Rafe Mazzeo, Solomon Quinn, Andras Vasy

item.title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.21964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks often learn low-frequency components before high-frequency ones --- a phenomenon called spectral bias or termed F-principle. Many numerical studies have demonstrated this phenomenon, and theoretical studies have sought to explain it. However, several goals remain insufficiently addressed: (1) explaining spectral bias asymptotically, including its origin and why the preferred components are generally sinusoidal; (2) extending the explanation to general activation functions, such as sigmoid and ReLU; (3) making weak assumptions about the data distribution; (4) avoiding aliasing effects, such as those arising in finite-domain Fourier analysis; and (5) developing a theoretical framework applicable to arbitrary networks. We address these goals theoretically by analyzing the eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes of the dynamics matrix H, which arises when we expand the network output as a general Fourier series (GFS) in an orthogonal polynomial basis and express the gradient-descent dynamics of the GFS coefficients as ordinary differential equations. The graded structure of H enables an intuitive explanation of spectral bias, while orthogonal polynomial theory helps us analyze how learning bias depends on the activation function and, potentially, the network architecture.
item.dc:creator: Yanyang Xiao

item.title: Convexity, the spectrum of free Laplacians and geometric consequences: a free KLS bound
item.description: arXiv:2610.22109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a compactness theorem for the resolvent of free Laplacians. More precisely, let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ be a self-adjoint tuple admitting Lipschitz conjugate variables in the sense of Dabrowski (2014). Under the non-commutative curvature--dimension condition $CD(c,\infty)$ with $c>0$, introduced in our previous work (2026), we prove that the free Laplacian $\Delta:=\partial^*\bar\partial$ is proper, that is, has compact resolvent. Our argument is non-perturbative and uses a spectral variant of the free Bochner method based on Dabrowski's almost-commutation formulas. A further stochastic argument gives a normal unital trace-preserving embedding of $M=W^*(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ into $L(\mathbb F_2)$. Together, the compactness and embedding theorems gives several operator-algebraic consequences, including the Haagerup approximation property, the CMAP, and strong solidity. We also obtain proper proximality and bi-exactness. We finally obtain several geometric consequences. We prove a free analogue of Klartag's improved log--Lichnerowicz inequality (2023), together with rigidity in the equality case. More surprisingly, under $CD(0,\infty)$, we prove a dimension-free Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits (KLS) bound in the free setting. As a consequence, we obtain a free thin-shell estimate for isotropic tuples. We conclude with further questions on spectral comparison with the canonical semicircular model.
item.dc:creator: Charles-Philippe Diez

item.title: Counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture near hyperbolic metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22281v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an LLM-assisted construction of counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture, with real analytic metrics arbitrarily close to a hyperbolic metric in dimension three. For acyclic unitary line characters tending to the trivial character, the modulus of the Ruelle zeta function at zero divided by analytic torsion squared tends to zero.
item.dc:creator: Simon Becker, Benjamin Lawton

item.title: Arbitrarily Fast Quantum Dispersion in Long-Range Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2608.27326v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct the first examples of one-dimensional long-range crystals exhibiting arbitrarily fast polynomial dispersive bounds. The Floquet functions of our Hamiltonians are highly oscillatory Weierstrass functions, whose rough autosimilar structure drives the fast dispersion. The proof develops a new Fourier decay theory for $C^\alpha$ images of the Lebesgue measure, based on a Dolgopyat-inspired transfer operator method, and yields a van der Corput lemma for Weierstrass functions. As a consequence, the local time of classical Weierstrass functions of sufficiently large lacunarity exists and is $C^k$, answering a question raised by Geman and Horowitz in 1980.
item.dc:creator: Ga\'etan Leclerc, Mostafa Sabri, Tuomas Sahlsten

item.title: Non-symmetric vector dyson equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.16333v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the vector Dyson equation $$-\frac{1}{m(z)}=z\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{a}+Sm(z),$$ with parameter $z$ in the complex upper half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+$, where $\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^d$ and $S$ is a nonnegative matrix, not necessarily symmetric. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. We also obtain the corresponding estimates for symmetric matrices in the periodic setting.
item.dc:creator: Jiaoyang Huang, Zhonggen Su, Ruizhe Xu

item.title: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators on smooth Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.06873v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a spectral representation theorem for compact operators that are self-adjoint with respect to the duality mapping on smooth Banach spaces. The result is a natural analogue of the classical spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators on Hilbert spaces.
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Shameem

item.title: Unique continuation at infinity for potentials with arbitrary radial growth
item.description: arXiv:2608.07276v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be any given continuous positive function on $\mathbb{R}_+$. Let $V$ be radial with $|V(x)|\leq G(|x|)$. We prove a Landis-type theorem for any real-valued solution of $\Delta u=Vu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We construct a decay threshold $e^{-g(r)}$, where $g$ is a strictly increasing function which can be computed explicitly in terms of $G$. Under suitable assumptions the exponent in the decay threshold is proportional to the Agmon distance associated with $G$.
item.dc:creator: Henrik Ueberschaer
